01_Signals_and_Systems_EAEPC302.name: Signals and Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: To understand the concept of signals and systems and their classifications.
CO2: To understand the concept of convolution and its applications.
CO3: To analyze the spectral characteristics of continuous-time and discrete-time periodic and aperiodic signals using Fourier analysis.
CO4: To analyze continuous-time LTI systems in the time domain and s-domain.
CO5: To analyze discrete-time LTI systems in the time domain and z-domain.
textbooks: Alan V. Oppenheim, Alan S. Willsky, S. Hamid Nawab, 'Signals and Systems', Prentice Hall India, 2nd Edition.
Simon Haykin and Barry Van Veen, 'Signals and Systems', John Wiley & Sons, 2nd Edition.
Tarun Kumar Rawat, 'Signals and Systems', Oxford University Press, 1st Edition.

units.title: Signal & System Fundamentals
topics: Concept definition & classification of signals (Continuous-time and Discrete-time)
Standard signals (Unit Step, Ramp, Rectangular Pulse, Impulse, Real and Complex Exponentials, Sinusoids)
Properties of unit impulse in continuous and discrete domain (Sifting property, Scaling property)
Concept of orthogonality of signals
Transformation of independent variables (Time shifting, Time scaling, Time reversal)
Classification of systems & properties (Linearity, Time-Invariance, Causality, Stability, Memory/Memoryless, Invertibility)
Waveform synthesis

units.title: LTI Systems & Convolution
topics: Continuous-time Convolution integral and its algebraic properties
Properties of Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Systems
Impulse response h(t) and Step response s(t)
Discrete-time Convolution sum and its properties
Graphical method of convolution for continuous and discrete signals
Interconnections of LTI systems (Cascade, Parallel)

units.title: Fourier Analysis (CTFS, DTFS, CTFT, DTFT)
topics: Continuous-Time Fourier Series (CTFS) representation of periodic signals and properties
Discrete-Time Fourier Series (DTFS) and its properties
Magnitude and Phase spectrum of periodic signals
Continuous-Time Fourier Transform (CTFT) and its properties (Duality, Time shifting, Frequency shifting, Parseval's relation)
Discrete-Time Fourier Transform (DTFT) and its properties
Magnitude and Phase representations of frequency response H(jω) of LTI systems
Introduction to Low-Pass (LP), Band-Pass (BP), High-Pass (HP), and All-Pass systems
Sampling Theorem and relationship between discrete-time signals and sampled continuous-time signals

units.title: Laplace Transform & Continuous LTI Systems
topics: Laplace Transform definition and Region of Convergence (ROC) properties
Inverse Laplace Transform (Partial Fraction Expansion method)
Unilateral Laplace Transform and its algebraic/calculus properties
Computation of impulse response, transfer function H(s), and differential equation solutions
Total system response (Zero-State Response ZSR and Zero-Input Response ZIR)
Stability and causality analysis of continuous-time LTI systems using pole-zero plots

units.title: Z-Transform & Discrete LTI Systems
topics: Z-Transform definition, Region of Convergence (ROC) and its properties
Inverse Z-Transform (Power series expansion, Partial fraction expansion, Contour integration)
Relationships between Z-Transform, Fourier Transform, and Laplace Transform
Stability and causality analysis of discrete-time LTI systems based on unit circle pole locations
Unilateral Z-Transform and difference equation solutions
Computation of discrete impulse response, transfer function H(z), Zero-State & Zero-Input responses

02_Probability_Theory_and_Random_Process.name: Probability Theory and Random Process
course_outcomes: CO1: To understand probability theory and random variables for the analysis of random phenomena.
CO2: To characterize probability models and functions of random variables based on single & multiple random variables.
CO3: To evaluate and apply moments & characteristic functions and understand the concept of inequalities.
CO4: To understand the concept of random processes and determine covariance and spectral density of stationary random processes.
CO5: To understand representation of low pass and band pass noise models.
textbooks: H. Stark and J. W. Woods, 'Probability and Random Processes with Applications to Signal Processing', 3rd Edition, Prentice Hall.
Athanasios Papoulis and S. Unnikrishna Pillai, 'Probability, Random Variables and Stochastic Processes', 4th Edition, McGraw-Hill.
P. Z. Peebles, 'Probability, Random Variables and Random Signals', 4th Edition, TMH.

units.title: Single Random Variables & Distributions
topics: Probability axioms, Conditional probability, Bayes' Theorem, Total Probability Rule
Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) and Probability Density Function (PDF) properties
Discrete, Continuous, and Mixed Random Variables
Standard Distributions: Uniform, Exponential, Normal (Gaussian), Rayleigh, Nakagami-m, Chi-Square
Discrete Distributions: Bernoulli, Binomial, Geometric, Poisson distribution
Mathematical Expectation, Variance, Standard Deviation, Raw and Central Moments
Moment Generating Function (MGF) and Characteristic Functions

units.title: Joint Random Variables & Random Vectors
topics: Bivariate & Joint CDF and Joint PDF
Marginal and Conditional distributions and Conditional Expectation
Statistical Independence, Uncorrelatedness, and Orthogonality of Random Variables
Covariance matrix, Correlation coefficient ρ, Cross-Moments
Joint Characteristic Functions and Joint MGF
Multidimensional Gaussian Law (Multivariate Normal Distribution, Covariance Matrix properties)

units.title: Functions of Random Variables & Inequalities
topics: Transformations of Single Random Variable Y = g(X)
Transformations of Joint Random Variables Z = g(X,Y), W = h(X,Y) and Jacobian determinant method
Sum of independent random variables and Convolution of PDFs
Chebyshev Inequality and Markov Inequality
Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality and Chernoff Bounds
Central Limit Theorem (CLT) and Laws of Large Numbers (Weak & Strong)

units.title: Random Processes & Stationarity
topics: Definition and Classification of Random (Stochastic) Processes
First-order and Second-order stationary processes
Wide-Sense Stationary (WSS) and Strict-Sense Stationary (SSS) processes
Time averages, Ensemble averages, and Ergodicity (Mean Ergodic and Correlation Ergodic processes)
Autocorrelation Function R_XX(τ) and its properties (Even symmetry, Maximum at zero lag, Periodic components)
Cross-Correlation Function R_XY(τ) and its properties
Autocovariance and Cross-Covariance functions
Discrete-time random processes and Markov chains

units.title: Spectral Density & LTI Systems with Random Inputs
topics: Power Spectral Density (PSD) S_XX(ω) and its physical interpretation/properties
Wiener-Khinchine Theorem (Fourier Transform relationship between R_XX(τ) and S_XX(ω))
Cross Power Spectral Density S_XY(ω)
Transmission of Random Processes through Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Systems
Output autocorrelation R_YY(τ) and output PSD S_YY(ω) = |H(ω)|² S_XX(ω)
White Noise process, Thermal noise, and Band-limited White Noise
Gaussian Random Processes and Narrowband Noise representation

03_Microelectronics_Circuits_and_Applica.name: Microelectronics Circuits and Applications
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe the small signal high frequency models of BJT and MOS transistors and use them in the frequency analysis of single-stage amplifiers.
CO2: Analyze differential and multi-stage amplifiers involving BJTs and MOSFETs.
CO3: Understand and describe the linear and nonlinear applications of op-amps and OTAs including filters and linear impedances etc.
CO4: Understand and elaborate the importance of negative feedback amplifier topologies and their characteristic features along with relevant analysis of positive feedback in sinusoidal oscillators.
CO5: Understand and describe power amplifiers and their realization involving power BJTs and Power MOSFETs.
textbooks: Adel S. Sedra and Kenneth C. Smith, 'Microelectronic Circuits', Oxford University Press, 1998 / 7th Edition.
P. R. Gray, P. J. Hurst, S. H. Lewis, and R. G. Meyer, 'Analysis and Design of Analog Integrated Circuits', 4th/5th Edition, Wiley.
Jacob Millman and Arvin Grabel, 'Microelectronics', McGraw-Hill, Inc., 1995.
Behzad Razavi, 'Design of Analog CMOS Integrated Circuits', McGraw-Hill, 2001.
P. E. Allen and D. R. Holberg, 'CMOS Analog Circuit Design', Oxford University Press, 2002.

units.title: Transistor Models & Frequency Response
topics: Review of Large-signal (DC) and Small-signal (AC) π-models and T-models for BJTs and MOSFETs
High-frequency hybrid-π models of BJT (C_π, C_μ, r_x, f_T) and MOSFET (C_gs, C_gd, f_T)
Biasing techniques in integrated circuit (IC) amplifiers: Simple current mirror, Wilson current mirror, Widlar current source
High-frequency response of Common-Source (CS) and Common-Emitter (CE) amplifiers (Miller effect, dominant pole)
High-frequency response of Common-Gate (CG) and Common-Base (CB) amplifiers with active loads
CS and CE amplifiers with source/emitter degeneration resistance
Source follower (CD) and Emitter follower (CC) frequency response
Low-frequency response of CE, CB, CC, CS, CG, CD amplifiers due to coupling/bypass capacitors

units.title: Multi-Stage & Differential Amplifiers
topics: Multi-stage amplifier configurations using MOSFETs and BJTs, Interstage coupling
Cascode amplifier topology (CS-CG, CE-CB), Output resistance boost, Gain-bandwidth product
Darlington pair configuration and CC-CE cascade
MOS Differential Pair: Large-signal DC transfer characteristics, Small-signal differential gain A_d, Common-mode gain A_cm, and CMRR
BJT Differential Pair: Large-signal operation, Differential and Common-mode analysis, Input resistance
Ideal and Non-ideal characteristics of differential amplifiers (Input offset voltage, offset current, temperature drift)
Differential amplifiers with active current mirror load (Single-ended conversion, A_d calculation)

units.title: Op-Amp & OTA Linear Applications
topics: Internal block diagram of general-purpose Operational Amplifier (Input stage, Gain stage, Level shifter, Output stage)
Operational Transconductance Amplifier (OTA) architecture and transconductance parameter g_m control
Linear Op-Amp circuits: Inverting amplifier, Non-inverting amplifier, Voltage follower, Difference amplifier, Instrumentation Amplifier
Mathematical operations: Summing amplifier, Subtractor, Practical Integrator (with DC stabilization), Differentiator (with high-frequency compensation)
Active Filters: First-order and Second-order Low-Pass, High-Pass, Band-Pass, and Band-Reject Butterworth filters (Sallen-Key topology)
Impedance synthesis and generalized impedance converters (GIC)
Linear applications of OTA (Voltage-controlled amplifiers, OTA-based filters)

units.title: Non-Linear Op-Amp Circuits, Timers & PLL
topics: Non-linear Op-Amp circuits: Logarithmic and Anti-logarithmic amplifiers using BJTs/diodes, Multipliers and Dividers
Analog Squarer and Square-rooter circuits, Precision half-wave and full-wave rectifiers, Peak detector
Waveform generators: Astable multivibrator, Monostable multivibrator, Bistable multivibrator (Schmitt Trigger with hysteresis)
Triangular and Sawtooth waveform generators using op-amp integrator and comparator loops
555 Timer IC: Internal architecture, Operation in Astable multivibrator mode (frequency and duty cycle design) and Monostable mode (pulse width)
Phase-Locked Loop (PLL 565): Block diagram, Phase detector, Loop filter, Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO 566), Lock range and Capture range
Function generator ICs (IC 8038 / XR2206 principles)

units.title: Feedback Topologies, Oscillators & Power Amplifiers
topics: General feedback concept: Advantages of negative feedback (Gain stabilization, Bandwidth extension, Noise reduction, Distortion reduction, Input/Output impedance modification)
Four basic feedback topologies: Voltage-Series (Series-Shunt), Voltage-Shunt (Shunt-Shunt), Current-Series (Series-Series), Current-Shunt (Shunt-Series)
Loop gain, Return ratio, Nyquist criterion, Gain Margin (GM) and Phase Margin (PM), Stability problem and Frequency compensation
Sinusoidal Oscillators: Barkhausen criterion for oscillation (Loop gain magnitude and phase condition)
RC Oscillators: RC Phase-shift oscillator and Wien-Bridge oscillator (Derivation of oscillation frequency and gain requirements)
LC Oscillators: Hartley oscillator, Colpitts oscillator, and Quartz Crystal oscillator (Piezoelectric effect, Series/Parallel resonance)
Power Amplifiers: Classification of output stages (Class A, Class B push-pull, Class AB complementary, Class C)
Efficiency, Maximum power dissipation, Crossover distortion and thermal runaway in Class B/AB stages
Power MOSFETs vs Power BJTs (Safe Operating Area SOA, Heat sinks, Discrete and IC power amplifiers)

04_Digital_Circuits_and_Systems_EAEPC305.name: Digital Circuits and Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: To get familiarized with number systems, codes, logic gates, logic families and Boolean algebra.
CO2: To analyze and understand the design process associated with combinational circuits.
CO3: To analyze and understand the design process associated with sequential circuits.
CO4: To understand fundamental concepts of VHDL modeling for basic digital circuits.
CO5: To develop basic understanding of programmable logic devices and converters.
textbooks: M. Morris Mano and Michael D. Ciletti, 'Digital Design: With an Introduction to the Verilog HDL, VHDL, and SystemVerilog', 5th/6th Edition, Pearson.
R. P. Jain, 'Modern Digital Electronics', 4th Edition, McGraw-Hill.
J. Bhasker, 'A VHDL Primer', 3rd Edition, Prentice Hall.

units.title: Number Systems, Boolean Algebra & Logic Families
topics: Digital design representations: Truth tables, Boolean equations, Schematic diagrams
Codes and properties: Weighted vs non-weighted codes, BCD (8421), Gray code (Binary-Gray conversion), Excess-3, Parity bits
Signed and unsigned binary numbers: Sign-magnitude, 1's complement, 2's complement arithmetic and overflow detection
Boolean algebra theorems: De Morgan's laws, Duality principle, Consensus theorem
Standard forms: Sum of Products (SOP), Product of Sums (POS), Canonical minterms (m) and maxterms (M)
Universal logic gates (NAND and NOR) and two-level NAND-NAND, NOR-NOR implementations
Logic Families: TTL and CMOS characteristics (V_IH, V_IL, V_OH, V_OL, Propagation delay, Noise Margin high/low, Fan-in, Fan-out, Power dissipation)
Interfacing: TTL driving CMOS and CMOS driving TTL with pull-up resistor calculation

units.title: Combinational Logic Design
topics: Karnaugh Maps (K-Maps) simplification up to 5 variables, Prime Implicants, Essential Prime Implicants, Don't Care conditions (d)
Tabulation Method (Quine-McCluskey Method) and Prime Implicant Chart reduction
Arithmetic circuits: Half Adder, Full Adder (using logic gates, NAND gates), Half Subtractor, Full Subtractor, Ripple Carry Adder, Look-Ahead Carry Adder
BCD Adder circuit design with correction logic (adding 6 when sum > 9 or carry generated)
Multiplexers (2:1, 4:1, 8:1, 16:1) and Boolean function implementation using Multiplexers
Demultiplexers and Decoders (2:4, 3:8, BCD to Decimal, BCD to 7-Segment decoder/driver)
Encoders and 8-to-3 Priority Encoders with valid bit
Magnitude Comparators (1-bit, 2-bit, 4-bit IC 7485 cascade)
Code converters (Binary to Gray, Gray to Binary, BCD to Excess-3)
Introduction to Programmable Read-Only Memory (PROM) for implementing arbitrary combinational logic

units.title: Sequential Logic Design & Finite State Machines
topics: Latches vs Flip-Flops: SR Latch (NOR/NAND gates), Gated SR Latch, D Latch, Race-around condition and Master-Slave JK Flip-Flop
Flip-Flop types: JK Flip-Flop, D Flip-Flop, T Flip-Flop, Truth tables, Characteristic equations, Excitation tables
Flip-Flop conversions (SR to JK, JK to D, D to T, etc.)
Registers and Shift Registers: Serial-In Serial-Out (SISO), Serial-In Parallel-Out (SIPO), Parallel-In Serial-Out (PISO), Parallel-In Parallel-Out (PIPO), Bidirectional Universal Shift Register
Asynchronous (Ripple) Counters: Modulo-N ripple counter, Up/Down ripple counters using T/JK flip-flops, Propagation delay limitation
Synchronous Counters: Modulo-N synchronous counter design, Arbitrary sequence counter design with self-starting analysis
Ring Counter and Johnson (Twisted Ring) Counter
Finite State Machine (FSM) models: Mealy Machine vs Moore Machine comparison
Synchronous Sequential Circuit Design: State diagram, State table, State reduction (Row elimination, Implication table), State assignment, Excitation & Output equations, Circuit realization

units.title: Hardware Description Language (VHDL)
topics: Motivation and methodology of modern digital hardware design using HDLs
VHDL Basic Structure: Entity declaration (port clause, modes: in, out, inout, buffer) and Architecture body
VHDL Libraries and packages (IEEE standard library, std_logic_1164, numeric_std)
Data types and objects: Signals, Variables, Constants, bit, std_logic, std_logic_vector, boolean, integer

VHDL Modeling Styles: Dataflow modeling (concurrent signal assignment, when-else, with-select-when), Structural modeling (component declaration, component instantiation, port map), Behavioral modeling (process statement, sensitivity list, if-then-else, case-when)
VHDL design implementations: Logic gates, 2:1 and 4:1 Multiplexers, Full Adder, 3:8 Decoder, D Flip-Flop with asynchronous/synchronous reset, 4-bit binary counter, Shift registers
Testbenches and simulation concepts

units.title: CMOS Gates, Data Converters & PLDs
topics: Transistor-level CMOS schematics: CMOS Inverter (voltage transfer characteristics, static power), CMOS NAND, CMOS NOR, CMOS Compound gates (AOI/OAI)
Digital-to-Analog Converters (DAC): Binary Weighted Resistor DAC, R-2R Ladder DAC (Inverted/Non-inverted), Resolution, Accuracy, Linearity, Settling time
Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADC): Flash (Simultaneous) ADC, Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC, Dual-Slope Integrating ADC, Counter-type ADC
Digital System Design using Algorithmic State Machine (ASM) charts and Datapath/Controller partitioning
Elements of CPU: ALU datapath, Register File, Control Unit logic
Programmable Logic Devices: Programmable Array Logic (PAL with fixed OR, programmable AND), Programmable Logic Array (PLA with programmable AND & OR), Generic Array Logic (GAL)
Complex Programmable Logic Devices (CPLD) and Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) architecture (CLB, IOB, Programmable interconnects, Look-Up Tables LUT)

05_Mathematics_For_Machine_Learning_EPMT.name: Mathematics for Machine Learning
course_outcomes: CO1: To understand the vector space and linear transformation.
CO2: To know the concept of inner product spaces and norms.
CO3: To know concept of matrix decomposition.
CO4: To know concept of vector calculus.
CO5: To know concept of optimization techniques.
textbooks: Marc Peter Deisenroth, A. Aldo Faisal, and Cheng Soon Ong, 'Mathematics for Machine Learning', Cambridge University Press, 2020.
Manaranjan Pradhan and U. Dinesh Kumar, 'Machine Learning using Python', Wiley, 2019.
Gilbert Strang, 'Linear Algebra and Its Applications', 4th Edition, Cengage Learning.

units.title: Linear Algebra & Linear Transformations
topics: Vector Spaces and Subspaces: Definition, Closure properties, Span of vectors
Linear Independence, Linear Dependence, and Linear Combinations
Basis of a vector space, Coordinates with respect to a basis, Dimension of a vector space
Linear Transformations: Definition, Properties, Kernel (Null Space) and Range (Column Space / Image)
Rank-Nullity Theorem (Fundamental Theorem of Linear Maps) and dimension calculations
Matrix representation of Linear Transformations with respect to standard and non-standard bases
Change of basis matrix and Similarity transformations

units.title: Matrix Theory, Inner Products & Eigenvalues
topics: Inner Product Spaces: Definition, Inner product axioms, Length/Norm of vectors, Angle and Orthogonality
Vector norms (L1, L2, L-infinity) and Matrix norms (Frobenius norm, Spectral norm)
Orthogonal Projections onto subspaces and Projection matrices
Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization Process and QR Decomposition
Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors: Characteristic polynomial, Algebraic and Geometric Multiplicities
Diagonalization of square matrices, Spectral Theorem for Symmetric Matrices
Orthogonal Matrices, Symmetric and Skew-Symmetric Matrices
Quadratic Forms: Matrix representation x^T A x, Canonical form, Principal Axis Theorem
Definiteness: Positive Definite, Positive Semi-Definite, Negative Definite, and Indefinite matrices (Sylvester's Criterion, Eigenvalue test)

units.title: Matrix Decomposition & Dimensionality Reduction
topics: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD): Geometric interpretation, Full and Compact SVD, Left singular vectors U, Singular values Σ, Right singular vectors V
Properties of Singular Values: Relationship to eigenvalues of A^T A and A A^T
Moore-Penrose Pseudo-Inverse A^+ and Minimum-norm Least Squares solutions
Low-Rank Matrix Approximations: Eckart-Young-Mirsky Theorem, Frobenius norm error of truncated SVD
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) derivation via SVD and Maximum Variance formulation
Polar Decomposition: Right Polar Decomposition (A = U P) and Left Polar Decomposition (A = P' U) where U is orthogonal and P is positive semi-definite

units.title: Vector Calculus & Integral Theorems
topics: Scalar and Vector functions in multiple dimensions, Contour lines and Level surfaces
Gradient vector ∇f: Geometric meaning as direction of steepest ascent, Directional Derivatives along unit vector u
Divergence ∇·F and Curl ∇×F of vector fields, Physical interpretation in solenoidal and irrotational fields
Jacobian Matrix for vector-valued functions and Chain Rule in multivariable calculus
Hessian Matrix ∇²f and Taylor Series expansion in multiple variables
Convex Sets and Convex Functions: Definition, Epigraph, First-order and Second-order convexity conditions (Positive semi-definite Hessian)
Line Integrals: Work done, Conservative vector fields, Potential functions and Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals
Surface Integrals and Volume Integrals
Integral Theorems: Green's Theorem in the plane, Stokes' Theorem in space, and Gauss Divergence Theorem (statements and applications)

units.title: Optimization Techniques & Support Vector Machines
topics: Unconstrained Optimization: First-Order Necessary Conditions (∇f(x*) = 0), Second-Order Sufficient Conditions (Hessian positive definite)
Iterative Optimization Methods: Gradient Descent, Steepest Descent, Learning rate / step size selection, Newton's Method, Quasi-Newton methods (BFGS)
Constrained Optimization: Equality constraints and Lagrange Multiplier formulation
Inequality constraints and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) Optimality Conditions (Primal feasibility, Dual feasibility, Complementary slackness, Stationarity)
Convex Optimization Problems and Duality Theory: Primal problem, Lagrangian Dual function, Weak and Strong Duality (Slater's condition)
Quadratic Programming (QP) problem formulation

Support Vector Machines (SVM): Maximum margin hyperplane formulation for linearly separable binary classification, Primal QP problem, Dual SVM derivation, Support vectors, Soft-margin C-SVM and Kernel trick introduction
